name: @circle-fin/daa-node-sdk
//private: Stays true in the repo. The release workflows flip it to false in the manifest they pack, so nothing can be published by accident from a checkout or a stray `pnpm publish`.
description: Server-side SDK for Digital Asset Accounts — the API-key authenticated endpoints
//engines: node >=22 matches the two current published @circle-fin wallets SDKs, which both declare it. Deliberately not >=18, even though the only hard requirement in the code is the global fetch that landed in Node 18 (see the guard in src/transport.ts): 18 is the floor below which this cannot work, not the floor Circle supports. The root manifest pins >=22.22.0 to mirror .nvmrc — that is a contributor pin, and consumers are deliberately held to the looser range. Treat a change to this range as a support-policy change, not a note: it is enforceable. Measured against npm 11.16.0 — a consumer with engine-strict=true has the install refused outright (EBADENGINE, exit 1), not warned. Without that setting npm warns and installs, and pnpm 10.34.5 says nothing at all.
